proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the premise-free repeated-star diagnostic and developed reusable Perron-order, finite-design Heyde--Brown, spectral-moment, and repeated-star combinatorial infrastructure. It stopped because the paper-owned boundary obstruction still needs a triangular-array Gaussian--Poisson mixture development, while prefix_flip_moments independently remains unproved; consequently every sorryAx-dependent field-level inference headline is excluded from this bank.
tldr: For the fixed \(r=2\) component-Perron Conflict Graph Design estimator, the sharp worst-case uniform normal-inference frontier is \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), with no additional slowly varying boundary factor. The proved quantitative bound is \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\{D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)+D_n/n\}^{1/5}\); repeated Perron-ordered stars give a legal non-normal convolution obstruction at the critical scale. The observable spectral variance-bound estimator is uniformly ratio-consistent in the normal regime and yields conservative feasible Wald coverage. In addition, the graph-adaptive condition \(D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\) is a sufficient pointwise rule for all three conclusions. Only the exact interior Kolmogorov rate, matched legal lower arrays for its vanishing terms, and optimized constants remain open.
gap: The published CGD theorem proves normality only under \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/9})\), while its counterexample lies in a much denser regime; later generic dependency bounds do not resolve the intervening CGD-specific range.
fill: The project tests the candidate prefix-sensitive martingale bound against legal critical repeated-star failures and, only if both survive D0, carries the resulting iff frontier through the observable spectral variance bound to conservative Wald coverage.
